claims.text: ADA recommends against antibiotics in most scenarios; antibiotics when systemic involvement or high risk of progression; DCDT prioritized in all cases
claims.quote: the panel recommended against using antibiotics in most clinical scenarios ... They recommended antibiotics in patients with systemic involvement (for example, malaise or fever) due to the dental conditions or when the risk of experiencing progression to systemic involvement is high.

claims.text: Definitive treatment includes root canal treatment or incision and drainage
claims.quote: definitive, conservative (tooth preserving) dental treatment (DCDT) (i.e. pulpotomy, pulpectomy, nonsurgical root canal treatment, or incision and drainage)

claims.text: Amoxicillin 500 mg three times a day or penicillin VK 500 mg four times a day, 3 to 7 days, plus urgent referral, for abscess with systemic involvement
claims.quote: The expert panel suggests dentists prescribe oral amoxicillin (500 milligrams, three times a day, 3–7d) or oral penicillin VK (500 milligrams, four times a day, 3–7d) for immunocompetent adults with pulp necrosis and acute apical abscess with systemic involvement.

claims.text: Non-response: add metronidazole or switch to amoxicillin-clavulanate, to enhance activity against Gram-negative anaerobes
claims.quote: For cases that do not respond promptly to antibiotics, clinicians may consider either complementing first-line treatment with oral metronidazole, or discontinue first-line treatment and prescribe oral amoxicillin/clavulanate, to enhance the efficacy against Gram negative anaerobic organisms.

claims.text: Metronidazole add-on 500 mg three times a day for 7 days
claims.quote: complement first-line treatment with oral metronidazole (500 milligrams, three times a day, 7d)

claims.quote: oral azithromycin (loading dose of 500 milligrams on day 1, followed by 250 milligrams for an additional four days)

claims.text: Clindamycin 300 mg four times a day 3 to 7 days (allergy with anaphylaxis/angioedema/hives)

claims.text: Systemic involvement = fascial space or local lymph node involvement, fever and/or malaise

claims.text: Benefits likely negligible, harms potentially large

claims.text: Oral antibiotics may not reach the affected tooth because of lack of vascular supply
claims.quote: oral antibiotics not reaching to the affected tooth because the lack of vascular supply
